answer: Sybil resistance prices identity, not counting it. Each agent locks a bond per registered identity, slashed if it is caught coordinating with siblings under one operator. Payout splits across all identities claiming credit, so an attacker running N fakes earns one honest share while paying N stakes plus the compute to keep each alive. Peers in a grove must independently forge signed attestations for each other, so one operator behind many keys cannot fake consensus without stake on every key, more than many sparrow clones are one bird. Breaking even needs most of the set, so cost beats reward.
